::: {.kw-overview}
Recurrent disease and graft survival lead this issue: an international TANGO analysis finds that the small minority of FSGS candidates with circulating anti-nephrin antibodies before transplantation recur early and often, and a Manchester cohort shows that biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy recurrence, although uncommon, cuts ten-year death-censored graft survival to roughly a third. On pharmacology, a Collaborative Transplant Study analysis of nearly 3,800 young recipients ties fast tacrolimus metabolism to graft loss in adolescents and young adults but not in younger children. For infection prevention, a phase 2b trial of the adjuvanted RSV prefusion F vaccine in kidney and lung recipients shows the vaccine is immunogenic and well tolerated, with mycophenolate blunting the first-dose response, which a second dose largely restores. A randomised trial in living-donor recipients finds no meaningful acid-base difference between saline and Plasma-Lyte under goal-directed fluid therapy, and a Groningen machine perfusion study delivers the TGF-β inhibitor galunisertib to discarded human kidneys during normothermic perfusion as a proof of concept against early fibrosis. Finally, two US papers on access and living donation describe how few veterans with advanced kidney disease move promptly through transplant evaluation, and how follow-up of living donors still falls short of national requirements, particularly for the donors at greatest long-term risk.
:::

---

### 1. [Anti-Nephrin Antibodies in Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis Recurrence After Transplantation: A Multicenter Study from the TANGO Consortium.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajt.2026.11.007)
[Lafargue MC, Hullekes F, Leon J, Verhoeff R, Gassen R, Mitra S, Fontanella AM, Mattiazzi AD, Burke GW, Fornoni A, Caridi G, Angeletti A, Moinuddin I, Gupta G, Reindl-Schwaighofer R, Huang E, Bugnazet M, Jouve T, Malvezzi P, Mansur J, Mastroianni-Kirsztajn G, Buxeda A, Pérez-Sáez MJ, Alenizi SA, Agena F, Araujo Silveira de Sa IJ, David-Neto E, Kitchens WH, Akalin E, Biancone L, Comai G, Bini C, La Manna G, Loupy A, Gallon L, Bodri N, Samland E, Seeger H, Cheng XS, Pawar AS, Krishnamoorthy S, Voora S, Hengel FE, Tomas NM, Huber TB, Uffing A, Berger SP, Leguern C, Anglicheau D, Cravedi P, Riella LV. *Am J Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 43035176.]{.kw-ref}

This brief communication from the international TANGO consortium drew on 49,536 kidney transplant recipients at 23 centres to identify 136 patients with biopsy-proven primary FSGS for whom stored pre-transplant serum was available. Anti-nephrin IgG was measured by ELISA, with a nested subset cross-checked by immunoprecipitation. Only 11 patients (8%) were antibody-positive, and they had been diagnosed much younger than the antibody-negative group (median 7 versus 26 years). Recurrence after transplantation affected 73% of antibody-positive patients against 38% of those without antibodies, a hazard ratio of 2.62 (95% CI 1.23 to 5.55), and in the positive group it appeared quickly, at a median of one month. Despite this, allograft failure did not differ significantly between the two groups over follow-up. The design is retrospective and the positive group is very small, so the estimates are imprecise. For UK units listing patients with primary FSGS, particularly those with childhood-onset disease, pre-transplant anti-nephrin testing looks like a promising way to identify candidates who may need close early proteinuria surveillance and a pre-agreed plan for recurrence, though it is not yet ready to guide routine listing decisions.

### 2. [Impact of recurrent IgA nephropathy on long-term kidney transplant outcomes: a cohort comparison with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12882-026-05207-2)
[Kamal R, Elewa M, Sevinc M, Carpio-Gonzalez I, Meghji M, Kanigicherla D. *BMC Nephrol*, 2026. PMID: 43009803.]{.kw-ref}

This retrospective study from the Manchester Royal Infirmary, for which the full text was available, compared 137 recipients transplanted for IgA nephropathy with 122 transplanted for ADPKD between 2010 and 2023, all managed on basiliximab induction with tacrolimus and mycophenolate and steroid withdrawal after five days. Median follow-up was 6.4 years in the IgAN group and 7.0 years in the ADPKD group. Taken as a whole, the two diseases had similar death-censored graft survival (78.1% versus 81.7% at ten years) and similar patient survival. However, 17 IgAN recipients (12.4%) developed recurrence confirmed on an indication biopsy, at a median of about five years, and their ten-year death-censored graft survival was 35.8% compared with 88.8% in those without recurrence (unadjusted HR 5.50, 95% CI 2.33 to 12.96). After recurrence, serum creatinine climbed by an extra 16.3 µmol/L per year relative to non-recurrent recipients, and recurrent disease was the recorded cause in 7 of the 21 IgAN graft losses. No pre-transplant factor, including HLA mismatch, predicted who would recur, and the small number of events ruled out multivariable modelling; because biopsies were done only for clinical indication, subclinical recurrence will have been missed. For UK practice, the data support counselling IgAN candidates that their early outcomes match those of other diagnoses, and maintaining long-term surveillance with a low threshold for biopsy, particularly as targeted IgAN therapies make treating recurrence a realistic prospect.

### 3. [Association of graft survival with tacrolimus metabolism in pediatric and young adult kidney transplant recipients: an international Collaborative Transplant Study analysis.](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00467-026-07619-6)
[Baghai Arassi M, Döhler B, Tönshoff B, Tran TH. *Pediatr Nephrol*, 2026. PMID: 43012923.]{.kw-ref}

Using the Collaborative Transplant Study database, the authors studied 3,768 tacrolimus-treated recipients aged 1 to 24 years, divided into children (1 to 11), adolescents (12 to 17) and young adults (18 to 24). The marker of interest was the tacrolimus concentration-to-dose ratio at one year, adjusted for body weight, which serves as a proxy for how quickly the drug is metabolised; the outcome was death-censored graft loss in years two to five. Adolescents and young adults lost grafts significantly more often than children. A ratio below 0.58, indicating fast metabolism, was independently linked to graft failure in adolescents (adjusted HR 1.74) and young adults (adjusted HR 1.98), whereas it made no difference in children. Fast metabolism was present in about a quarter of adolescents (25.2%) and 13.8% of young adults, and among young adults its association with graft loss was stronger in those who were sensitised before transplantation. The analysis is retrospective and observational. For UK paediatric and transition services, the one-year concentration-to-dose ratio is a cheap, already-available signal that could help flag adolescents and young adults who need closer tacrolimus monitoring or a review of their formulation.

### 4. [AS01_E_-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78584-9)
[Small C, Kumar D, Abbas A, Sánchez Fructuoso A, Yamanaga S, Pérez González VL, Karakizlis H, Nissen M, Gyun Choe P, Paloschi V, Chadban S, Hailemariam HA, Gerard C, David MP, Descamps D, Vandermeulen C, Oluwayi K, Hulstrøm V, RSV OA=ADJ-023 Study Group. *Nat Commun*, 2026. PMID: 43026212.]{.kw-ref}

This open-label, multinational phase 2b trial, read in full text, randomised adult kidney or lung recipients who were at least a year from transplantation and stable on maintenance immunosuppression to one dose (n = 131) or two doses 30 to 60 days apart (n = 130) of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine; about 70% in each arm were kidney recipients, and 125 non-immunocompromised adults aged 50 or over received a single dose as a reference group. For the primary endpoint, a second dose raised RSV-A and RSV-B neutralising titres modestly further, with geometric mean increases of 1.34 (95% CI 1.20 to 1.48) and 1.26 (1.14 to 1.40) relative to the first dose. A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients but produced slower and lower initial responses than in controls, a deficit concentrated in the roughly three-quarters taking mycophenolate; in that subgroup a second dose brought titres into a range similar to the controls after one dose. Vaccine-specific CD4 T-cell responses rose in all groups, and both humoral and cellular responses stayed above baseline for 12 months. Reactogenicity was similar to that in controls, with grade 3 solicited reactions in 3.9% or fewer of participants; serious adverse events were more common in the transplant arms, as expected in this population, and only one was judged vaccine-related. The trial measured immune responses rather than protection against RSV disease. For UK transplant clinics, the data support offering adjuvanted RSV vaccination to established kidney recipients and suggest that a second dose may be worth considering for patients on mycophenolate.

### 5. [Comparison of the effects of normal saline versus Plasma-Lyte® on acid-base balance during living donor kidney transplantation surgery using goal-directed fluid therapy based on pulse pressure variation- a randomised controlled trial.](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12871-026-04148-5)
[Kumar S, Loganathan S, Kajal K, Gandhi K, Sethi S, Sharma A, Garg K, Ray A, Mahajan V, Singh S. *BMC Anesthesiol*, 2026. PMID: 43026518.]{.kw-ref}

In this prospective, assessor-blinded randomised trial from India, adults undergoing living-donor kidney transplantation received either normal saline or Plasma-Lyte intraoperatively, with volumes titrated to a pulse pressure variation algorithm. Acid-base status was analysed with the Stewart approach, and the primary endpoint was apparent strong ion difference. Among 111 analysed patients (55 saline, 56 Plasma-Lyte), total intraoperative fluid was moderate and similar between arms (about 1.8 to 1.9 litres). Strong ion difference fell over the course of surgery in both groups without any between-group difference; the adjusted difference at the end of surgery was 0.71 mmol/L (90% CI −0.90 to 2.32), so formal equivalence within the pre-set ±2 mmol/L margin was not demonstrated. pH, potassium, lactate and other Stewart variables were similar throughout, as were early graft dysfunction (4.1% versus 7.4%), delayed graft function (3.6% versus 0%) and creatinine trajectories, although the study was not powered for graft outcomes. The setting was living donation, with low delayed graft function rates and modest fluid volumes. For UK anaesthetic and surgical teams, the trial suggests that, at the moderate volumes given here under a goal-directed protocol, the haemodynamic strategy may shape acid-base status more than the choice of crystalloid; whether this holds for higher-volume deceased-donor cases was not tested.

### 6. [Galunisertib During Normothermic Machine Perfusion Attenuates Profibrotic Signaling in Discarded Human Donor Kidneys.](https://doi.org/10.1111/aor.70281)
[Pamplona CC, Ballester Bergada C, Jaynes CL, Hamelink TL, Lantinga VA, Ogurlu B, Ottens P, Olinga P, van Hateren K, Touw D, Hillebrands JL, Leuvenink HGD, Moers C, van Leeuwen LL. *Artif Organs*, 2026. PMID: 43053590.]{.kw-ref}

The Groningen perfusion group asked whether normothermic machine perfusion could serve as a route for giving an antifibrotic drug directly to a donor kidney. Twelve human kidneys declined for transplantation underwent 4 hours of oxygenated hypothermic perfusion and then 6 hours of normothermic perfusion with either the TGF-β receptor inhibitor galunisertib or vehicle (six per arm). Precision-cut slices from each kidney were then cultured for 48 hours with or without continued drug exposure. Galunisertib was cleared steadily into the urine during perfusion, and ex vivo renal function was not adversely affected. When exposure continued in the slices, expression of fibrosis-related genes fell, including SERPINE1 at 24 and 48 hours; stopping the drug was followed by a rise in ACTA2 expression that continued treatment prevented. The authors describe the antifibrotic effect as modest, and the endpoints are molecular markers in discarded organs rather than graft outcomes. For UK centres building normothermic perfusion programmes, the study is an early proof of concept that the perfusion circuit could carry targeted therapies to the organ without systemic exposure, though clinical benefit remains untested.

### 7. [Varied trajectories through the transplant evaluation process: Results of a sequence analysis among a national cohort of Veterans with advanced kidney disease.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajt.2026.11.001)
[Butler CR, Pessin L, Blankenhorn RK, Carey EP, Eyre H, Prince DK, Reese PP, O'Hare AM. *Am J Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 43014621.]{.kw-ref}

This national retrospective cohort followed 39,691 US veterans whose eGFR first fell to 20 mL/min/1.73 m² or below between October 2011 and December 2018, tracking their passage through the transplant process over five years using sequence analysis. The cohort was older (median age 70.1) and almost entirely male (97.2%). Seven distinct pathways emerged: death early in follow-up was the commonest (50.5%), and for a further 24.6% transplantation was never mentioned in the record. Smaller groups declined to pursue it (6.2%), deliberated for a long time (4.6%) or remained in evaluation for a prolonged period (8.9%), while only 3.3% were waitlisted promptly and 1.9% were transplanted promptly. Older age, greater comorbidity and higher neighbourhood deprivation were associated with being less likely to progress promptly and more likely to stall at early steps or never engage. The population was older and predominantly male, which should be kept in mind when applying the findings elsewhere. For UK services working to widen access, the study is a reminder that increasing referrals will help only if the evaluation that follows is streamlined and paired with structured shared decision-making.

### 8. [Landscape Of Post-Donation Follow-up of Living Kidney Donors in the United States, 2013-2023.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajt.2026.10.027)
[Reed RD, Xue R, Thomas AG, Akhtar J, Menon G, Weiss S, Segev DL, Stewart DE, Orandi BJ, Ali NM, Stern JM, Massie AB, Levan ML. *Am J Transplant*, 2026. PMID: 43003187.]{.kw-ref}

Using OPTN data on 64,488 living kidney donors from February 2013 to December 2023, the authors measured how often follow-up was submitted completely and on time, as defined by OPTN policy, at six months, one year and two years after donation. Rates hardly changed across the decade. Complete and timely clinical data were submitted for 84%, 81% and 75% of donors at the three time points, and laboratory data for 80%, 75% and 68%. Donors with a pre-donation BMI of 30 or more, Black donors and younger donors were more likely to have incomplete follow-up at every time point. Performance also varied considerably by centre, with the proportion of programmes meeting the six-month threshold ranging from 56% to 81% in different years. The analysis is a retrospective review of registry submissions. For UK living donor programmes, the study is a prompt to audit lifelong follow-up and to target retention efforts at donors who carry the highest long-term risk of kidney disease.
